key_insight: Adaptive hyperreduction accelerates neural constitutive model discovery from structural experiments while preserving identification accuracy in the reported examples.
engineering_relevance: Engineers can identify material laws from reaction-force data without measuring full displacement fields, accommodating complex geometries and boundary conditions.
method: Combine proper orthogonal decomposition with energy-conserving sampling and weighting.
Adapt reduced trial spaces and sampled elements during optimization, using reduced-model adjoint sensitivities.
Use a neural strain-energy model that enforces polyconvexity, coercivity, and non-negativity by construction.
evidence_signal: Across two experimental datasets and one synthetic 3D example, the method reproduced reaction forces and predicted displacement fields; two-phase specimen training fell from 9 hours to 41 minutes without reported accuracy loss.
watch_item: Accuracy depends on keeping the reduced basis and element sampling representative as the neural material changes during training.
paper_title: Hyperreduction accelerates finite element model updating for the discovery of neural materials
